question.text: Which of the following is TRUE about open-ended Category III AIFs?

answer.text: They cannot accept capital after initial offer period
Redemption is permitted only at winding-up
First single lump-sum investment from an investor must be at least Rs. 1 crore; partial redemptions must not reduce holding below Rs. 1 crore
Minimum lock-in of 3 years on all investments

explanation.text: The Logic: For open-ended Cat III AIFs, the first lump-sum investment cannot be less than Rs. 1 crore, and post partial redemption the investor's remaining holding must also stay at ≥ Rs. 1 crore. The Trap: Open-ended funds DO accept capital post Initial Offer Period. Redemption is permitted at pre-defined regular intervals, not only at winding-up. Cross-Exam Context: Unique to open-ended Cat III — Cat I/II (XIX-A) are mandatorily close-ended. Distributor's Pro-Tip: When advising partial redemption, check that residual capital stays ≥ Rs. 1 crore — fund might have to reject the request otherwise.
